title: SD card protocol
summary: SD cards use SPI or SD bus (1-bit or 4-bit). Initialization: CMD0 (GO_IDLE_STATE), CMD8 (SEND_IF_COND), ACMD41 (SD_SEND_OP_COND), CMD2 (ALL_SEND_CID), CMD3 (SEND_RELATIVE_ADDR), CMD9 (SEND_CSD), CMD7 (SELECT_CARD). Data transfer: CMD17 (READ_SINGLE_BLOCK), CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK), CMD24 (WRITE_SINGLE_BLOCK), CMD25 (WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK). Status: R1 (1 byte), R3 (5 bytes, for ACMD41), R7 (5 bytes, for CMD8).

structure.meaning: 0x40 + arg (0) + CRC. Puts card in idle state.
0x48 + arg (voltage + check pattern). Checks if card supports 3.3V and returns echo.
0x69 (CMD41 with APP_CMD prefix 0x37). Initializes card. Arg: host capacity support (HCS) + voltage window.
0x43 + arg (0). Returns RCA (Relative Card Address, 16 bits).
0x49 + arg (RCA). Returns CSD (Card Specific Data, 128 bits: capacity, speed, etc.).
0x47 + arg (RCA). Selects card for data transfer.
Status: in_idle_state, erase_reset, illegal_command, crc_error, erase_sequence_error, address_error, parameter_error.
Capacity, max speed, read/write block sizes, erase sizes, etc.
Manufacturer ID, OEM ID, product name, product revision, serial number, manufacturing date.

notes: SD cards use SPI mode (1-bit) or SD mode (1-bit/4-bit).
SD cards support up to 2TB (SDXC) or 32GB (SDHC).
SD card initialization takes ~1-2 seconds (ACMD41 polling).
SD cards have wear leveling and bad block management internally.
SD cards are used in cameras, phones, Raspberry Pi, and many embedded systems.
